corrections: The getter routines are seven bytes each: six-byte LEA plus RET.
The codec does not end at its first RET (0x5C2562): loop bodies continue through 0x5C25FE, followed by a four-entry jump table at 0x5C2600..0x5C260F. The adjacent routine begins at 0x5C2610.

The original codec has behavior beyond ordinary Windows-1252 conversion: mapped value 0xFF emits '?' but does not clear the success flag, because emission uses unsigned <0xFF while failure uses >0xFF.
The MP3 ID3v2 copy loads through pointer arrays: [tag+4] or [tag+8], then their first pointer. It uses imported strncpy with count 256; this alone does not guarantee termination.
The UTF-8 copy and field-scoped bridge changes are intentional modifications. Their reported tests and private live traces do not establish recovered original behavior.
ParseOctane.dll and the private logs were unavailable. Their token bodies, range arithmetic and live observations remain unverified here.

findings.hint: Recover the codec's scalar-to-Windows-1252 mapper first. This small dependency takes a scalar in ECX, returns EAX, maps special Windows-1252 characters, and otherwise returns the input unchanged.
evidence: Original disassembly shows a complete conditional chain beginning with U+20AC -> 0x80 and ending with U+0178 -> 0x9F; the final fallback is mov eax,ecx; ret.
Multiple early returns belong to this same chain; padding starts at 0x5C24FD.
No corresponding address/name was found in searched recovered source or native registry; registry interval inspection found no covering entry.
validation_plan: Compare original and recovered EAX for every special mapping, all values 0..255, U+2010, nearby unmapped scalars, supplementary values and unsigned extremes.
Check preserved registers and absence of memory writes.
limits: Register ABI is established from the inspected call and instructions; no independent symbol name was established.

findings.hint: Recover the original lossy codec with its actual length convention, decoder tables, output-string mutations and success flag. Preserve its quirks instead of substituting a standard UTF-8 decoder.
evidence: Original metadata identifies elCodec.UTF8ToWindows1252 as native unmanaged cdecl(input pointer, uint32 length, std::string&), returning an unsigned-byte bool.
Entry bytes are 55 8B EC 83 EC 0C. String length is at +0x10, capacity at +0x14; capacity >=16 selects heap storage.
0x5C2532 treats length 0xFFFFFFFF as NUL-terminated mode. Explicit-length mode checks source+trailing-byte-count against the end pointer before decoding.
The decoder uses byte table 0x9F3310, subtraction table 0x9F3410 and jump table 0x5C2600; calls scalar mapper 0x5C2380 and append member 0x442170.
0x5C25A9..0x5C25BA substitutes '?' unless the mapped value is unsigned <255; 0x5C25E6..0x5C25FA clears accumulated success only for values >255.
Native registry has no covering codec entry. Append dependency 0x442170 already has recovered C++ in batches/source-397.
dependencies: Original tables at 0x9F3310 and 0x9F3410, including legacy five/six-byte lead classifications
VA 0x442170 narrow append and its existing allocation/alias dependencies
Original 24-byte native narrow-string ABI and allocator
validation_plan: Compare original return byte, output bytes, length, terminator and guarded string storage for ASCII, empty input, U+2010, Windows-1252 special mappings, U+00FF and CJK.
Exercise explicit lengths versus 0xFFFFFFFF, exact-end and truncated sequences, embedded NULs, malformed continuation bytes, and inline/heap output storage.
Use padded guarded input when investigating speculative reads; preserve observed original behavior separately from proposed fixes.
limits: Static inspection only; the note's BUCK?TICK execution result was not rerun.
Complete allocation failure, aliasing and malformed-input behavior remains to be validated.

findings.hint: Use the original IL as a larger recovery roadmap after recovering its small dependencies. Preserve response conversion, acceptance branches, request reset, string ownership and exception cleanup in faithful source.
evidence: Original method table row 5342 corresponds to token 0x060014DE. Emitted IL reports RVA 0x34FE9C, code size 0x622 and maxstack 8.
IL_0089 obtains bodyToString into local 48; IL_00A6..00C4 selects its native storage, loads its length, calls UTF8ToWindows1252 into local 47 and discards the bool.
IL_00E9 parses local 47. IL_021F/026F/02B6/02F6 reads artist/name.
IL_0247 selects object offset 480 decimal (0x1E0). Comparison and non-placeholder checks precede IL_0323 assigning the response artist.
Fault handlers and normal _Tidy calls clean locals 46/47/48; elJSON destruction occurs on normal and fault paths.
Later IL updates other screen fields, invokes virtual calls and emits Track_Converted analytics; this is not merely a conversion wrapper.

review.summary: Approved as assembly-reference evidence for VA 0x5C2380–0x5C24FC. The complete conditional chain extends beyond the first return; on the U+0178 path it also changes ECX to 0x9F before returning that value in EAX. This is not source recovery or evidence of the surrounding codec’s behavior.
review.reason: Independently assembled all 381 symbolic instruction bytes and compared them unmasked with the corresponding Game.exe bytes; they match. Disassembly confirms the branches, final return, adjacent padding, caller’s ECX/EAX use, and absence of external calls or data dependencies. The original and candidate hashes match the receipts, and the reference registry shows no overlapping entry. No execution-based behavior validation or compiler-built source credit is claimed.
